medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The College values diversity in its medical education programs. Individuals from different backgrounds and experiences not only enhance the quality of education for all students, but also translate into graduates who are more effective and better prepared to serve multiple patient populations. UTHSC College of Medicine actively encourages applications from members of groups who are underrepresented in medicine (e.g., students from groups underrepresented in medicine, rural areas, disadvantaged socioeconomic or educational backgrounds, or students with past or present military service). The Committee on Admissions evaluates nonacademic, as well as, academic factors in the selection process, with consideration being given to the unique backgrounds and challenges of these applicants.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Leaves of absence are considered for students for both academic and personal reasons.  The Office of Student Affairs, in conjunction with the Office of Medical Education, considers these requests.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: The Medical Student Executive Council, Phi Chi Medical Fraternity, SNMA, AMSA, OSR, AMA, Honor Council, Professionalism Committee, Council on International and Area Outreach, Women in Medicine and Science, UT Unite (LGBTQI), and Specialty Interest Groups are available to students.  We offer a full range of intramural programs and exercise facilities. Students serve on all major College committees.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: UTHSC is situated in one of the largest medical centers in the nation and close to vibrant downtown Memphis, home of NBA basketball, AAA baseball, the Symphony, Broadway plays, Beale St. blues and barbecue.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: An abundance of off-campus housing is available. See https://www.uthscoffcampus.com/
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Through the Office of Student Affairs, the College of Medicine provides support for all students including gender and sexual minority students. In addition, Unite is a student-led campus organization that aims to improve the visibility, strength and support of LGBTQI students.  The Office of Student Counseling Services is also involved in providing strong support for LGBTQI students.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
The Office of Academic Success provides quality programming, services, and resources to assist students in adjusting to the emotional, academic, social, and physical demands of the health science curricula and health care professions. Through this office, methods, resources, and techniques, the environment is enriched to support adjustment, coping, learning and performance. The Office of Academic Success services are available free of charge to all UTHSC students and are available in person, over the phone, and/or online for students at each campus location. Additionally, the College of Medicine has a Medical Student Wellness Committee which is student-led committee and bridges the gap between life in medical school and wellness. This goal is accomplished by focusing on six aspect of wellness: physical, emotional, spiritual, social, professional, and intellectual. We present and regularly update information that pertains to these six aspects and organize group events to promote student wellness.

The UTHSC College of Medicine is devoted to providing a training environment in which students’ educational and work requirements can be balanced with family and life obligations and the maintenance of student’s physical and mental health. This is codified in the Excused Absence and Wellness Days policy which delineates the mechanisms available to students when learning is disrupted by acute illness, which would fall under an excused absence, but it also provides students with the ability to take discretionary wellness days that need not be explained.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The Office of Academic Success provides a wide range of services including tutoring, test preparation, board preparation, and learning styles inventories.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Integrated class content, flipped classroom style, team-based learning, simulation, and clinical correlations.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations begin in February or March of the second year.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The UT Health Science Center College of Medicine (COM) is Tennessee’s flagship medical school with campuses in Memphis, Nashville, Chattanooga, and Knoxville. Preclinical training occurs in Memphis. The MD curriculum begins with an integrated foundational science phase covering gross anatomy with full‑body dissection, embryology, histology, biochemistry, genetics, and related sciences. Principles of Clinical Medicine (PCM) spans all four years, building clinical and communication skills through standardized patients, simulation, ultrasound, and early clinical exposure. Students work with inpatient and outpatient preceptors to connect foundational learning to patient care.

In the first year, students progress through foundational sciences and mechanisms of disease. In the spring, they enter an organ‑system curriculum integrating physiology, pathology, pharmacology, microbiology, and pathophysiology for the rest of the preclinical phase. Dedicated USMLE Step 1 preparation occurs in January and February of M2 with individualized study time.

Clinical training begins in the second semester of M2, with core clerkships starting as early as February or March. The third year includes core clerkships and career‑exploration rotations, allowing greater responsibility in patient care and decision‑making. Step 2 CK preparation may begin in the spring of M3.

The post‑clerkship phase offers flexibility through elective rotations, junior internships, away rotations, and an eight‑week Flex Block supporting research, scholarly work, or individualized goals. This structure helps students strengthen residency applications and explore specialties.

The COM offers a four‑year MD program, an accelerated three‑year track for students committed to a specialty and UTHSC residency, and dual‑degree options including MD/PhD, MD/MBA, and MD/MPH in partnership with the University of Memphis and St. Jude. Research opportunities remain available through flexible pathways.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: The COM has a strong commitment to training physicians with interest in primary care. Throughout the 4-year curriculum, students are exposed to primary care options through preceptors and master clinicians in the first two years and during clerkships, electives, and junior internships in the clinical phase of the curriculum. The accelerated 3-year curriculum is available to students who plan to enter a primary care residency program at UTHSC upon completion of the MD degree.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Founded in 1911, the College of Medicine is one of six (6) Colleges that comprise the University of Tennessee Health Science Center (UTHSC). The College’s statewide programs are located on four (4) fully integrated locations - Memphis, Knoxville, Nashville and Chattanooga, as well as smaller sites across the state of Tennessee. Many of the nation’s top leaders in research and clinical medicine have trained at UTHSC.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Transforming lives through collaborative and inclusive education, research/scholarship, clinical care, and public service is the mission of the University of Tennessee Health Science Center.

The College of Medicine aims to improve the health of Tennesseans and our society as a whole by providing an exceptional and nurturing environment for the education of students and physicians, by contributing to advances in medical science, and by providing health services of the highest quality.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Consistent with AAMC's Choose Your Medical School Timeline
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Applicants should submit three (3) letters of reference with at least two (2) from science professors. The third letter can be a non-academic reference. Evaluation letters should address areas such as personal characteristics, problem solving abilities, specific areas of strength, special experiences, leadership experiences, decision-making skills, communication skills, work habits, attitude and character.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Two individual interviews with admissions committee members.  One interview is academic in nature while the other focuses on the personal aspects of the applicant. Interviews last 30.
medSchoolApplication.regionalInterview: The College of Medicine Committee on Admissions includes faculty from regional campuses. Candidates may be interviewed by one of those committee members.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: The College of Medicine will continue to host interviews virtually throughout the entire 2027 admissions cycle.
medSchoolApplication.secApplEarliestDtText: Once we have received a verified application from AMCAS, only a select group of applicants will be sent a link to complete the secondary application
medSchoolApplication.secApplLatestDtText: The deadline to submit the secondary application is seven (7) days after the invitation has been extended.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: Students from any state may apply (10% limit on admitted nonresidents). Preference is given to Tennessee residents.  US citizenship or permanent residency is required at the time of application.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Preference is given to Tennessee residents; only 10% of the entering class may be from out of state.
medSchoolApplication.transferContact: Dr. Dustin Fulton, Assistant Dean For Admissions
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: Total MCAT scores at or above the 50th percentile are considered more competitive.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: BCPM or Science GPAs at or above 2.5 are generally more competitive.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: UTHSC College of Medicine will accept prerequisite academic work from any accredited institution, including community colleges, as long as applicants meet other necessary requirements and have completed upper level coursework at a four-year institution leading to a bachelor's degree.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Generally, letters of intent or update letters are reserved for candidates who have been invited for an interview.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
Students in the UTHSC College of Medicine must possess the following general qualities: critical thinking, sound judgment, emotional stability empathy, physical and mental stamina, and the ability to learn and perform tasks in a wide variety of educational and clinical settings. In all phases of medical education, students must use their intellectual ability and must maintain emotional stability, particularly when under stress. Graduates of the College of Medicine must have the knowledge and skills to function in a broad variety of clinical situations and to render a wide spectrum of patient care.

The College of Medicine requires that students meet certain minimum technical standards, with or without accommodation. These standards must be met for matriculation and maintained throughout a student’s enrollment and graduation.  We encourage all prospective students to review our Technical Standards for Admission, Progression and Graduation at the link below.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Aid consists of loans, scholarships, and work-study.  Merit- and need-based scholarships are available to students. Detailed financial aid information can be found at: https://www.uthsc.edu/medicine/student-affairs/scholarships.php

medSchoolMdPathway.programDesc: UTHSC’s 3-year MD program allows students to complete medical school in three years while meeting all graduation requirements (>130 curriculum weeks). Students are accepted at matriculation or during spring of the M1 year, and transition directly into UTHSC residencies upon graduating. The program has a mission to reduce student debt, increase mentorship, and retain physicians in Tennessee. There are also off ramps to transition back into the 4-year program.
medSchoolMdPathway.spotAvailable: The program admits up to 14 students at matriculation, with up to 17 students total, including those accepted during the spring of the M1 year.
medSchoolMdPathway.eligibleApplicants: Applicants to the 3-year MD program  must be first admitted to the College of Medicine through the regular admissions process.
medSchoolMdPathway.applicationDeadline: Applications are typically submitted by the end of January, either prior to matriculation or during the spring of the M1 year.
medSchoolMdPathway.applicationProcess: Applicants submit AMCAS materials to the 3-year MD committee, along with a one-page essay outlining their interest in and experience with the intended specialty. Selected applicants are invited to interview with both the 3-year MD committee and the affiliated residency program. Admission requires approval from both and includes a directed pathway to a UTHSC residency.
medSchoolMdPathway.residencyAffiliationPathway: Directed residency option for all Three-Year MD students
medSchoolMdPathway.resAdditionalInfo: Medicine-Pediatrics and Pediatric Neurology are also available residency pathways at UTHSC. These options are not shown in the drop-down menu provided.
medSchoolMdPathway.residencySlots: While there is no fixed number of slots per residency program, each participating residency program retains full discretion in selecting applicants. Total enrollment in the 3-year program is capped at 17 students per year.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Applicants should acquire a comprehensive pre-medical preparation. Although Psychology, Sociology and Biochemistry are not required courses for matriculation, these courses have always been strongly recommended in preparation for the MCAT and medical curriculum. Additional dimensions are derived from higher mathematics, computer sciences, languages, literature, philosophy, history, political science, economics, etymology and statistics. Regardless of choice of major, applicants are encouraged to pursue a course of study which achieves a balance between both science and non-science coursework.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: For prerequisite coursework older than five years, the admissions committee may require additional upper division biological science course work.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The criteria the Committee on Admissions uses in the selection process are the academic record, MCAT scores, pre-professional evaluations, and personal interviews. Personal interviews by members of the committee provide candidates with an opportunity to review their academic and extracurricular activities and how they have formulated their plans for the study and practice of medicine. The University of Tennessee Health Science Center College of Medicine will give priority for admission to applicants from the State of Tennessee. Applicants from any state may apply and be considered for admission, but priority will continue to be given to Tennessee residents. A small number (currently 10% of each class) of out-of-state applicants may be admitted. When out-of-state applicants are admitted, preference will be given to the children of University of Tennessee alumni. Applicants must be citizens or permanent residents of the United States at the time of application.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: The Committee of Admissions considers it vital that prospective applicants enhance their knowledge of medicine through direct, patient-oriented clinical experience in a variety of settings. Such experience, which is frequently gained through volunteer work, should enable the applicant to acquire a greater understanding of the realities of medicine and provide an opportunity for service.
